blogsMeta.headline: Notes from inside real systems
blogsMeta.intro: Things I have had to work out on production systems, written down while the detail is still fresh. Mostly commerce architecture, backend engineering and the trade-offs that only show up under load.

posts.title: Your checkout needs idempotency keys
posts.summary: Retries without idempotency do not make a payment flow resilient. They make it charge people twice. Here is the design that actually holds.

posts.title: OCAPI or SCAPI: choosing without regretting it later
posts.summary: The two Salesforce Commerce APIs overlap enough to look interchangeable and differ enough to make the wrong pick a migration. A practical way to decide.

posts.title: Cache invalidation is a correctness problem
posts.summary: Teams add caching to fix latency and quietly accept a class of bugs they never wrote down. Invalidation deserves the same rigour as the query it replaces.

posts.title: Reading a JVM heap dump without panicking
posts.summary: A service is using four gigabytes and nobody knows why. A repeatable process for getting from that sentence to the offending line of code.

posts.title: Structured outputs are most of the work
posts.summary: The difference between an LLM demo and an LLM feature is almost entirely in the contract between the model and the code that consumes it.

posts.title: Cut services along domain seams, not team charts
posts.summary: Most painful microservice migrations split the system where the org chart was, not where the data ownership was. The difference shows up in every transaction afterwards.
